steps.text: Preheat oven to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C).
In a small bowl, combine the milk and salt. In a separate bowl, mix together the bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and thyme.
Dip the haddock fillets in the milk, then press into the crumb mixture to coat. Place haddock fillets in a glass baking dish, and drizzle with melted butter.
Bake on the top rack of the preheated oven until the fish flakes easily, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Haddock
raw_recipe.description: This baked haddock recipe is quick and easy to prepare with a Parmesan bread crumb coating for a kid-friendly dinner in less than 30 minutes!

video.description: Are you on the hunt for the best baked fish recipe? Fortunately, your search ends here. In this video, learn how to make baked haddock, the perfect recipe for those hurried weeknight meals. This seafood recipe is quick and easy to prepare using a Parmesan bread crumb coating, and it makes a healthier alternative to deep frying without sacrificing flavor. We think everyone at your table will love this wonderful meal.

review.reviewBody: Love this reciept. To prevent the soggy bottom I put the fish on a cooling wire rack and then set it in the baking dish,I also squeezed a little fresh lemon on it before it went in to the oven. it came out nice and crisp on both sides. My family loved it.

VERY GOOD!!! There's a popular restaurant back home in Boston whose website lists this same recipe for their Baked Haddock. It is delicious! It'll work just fine with a variety of fish; you could use tilapia, orange roughy or cod as well as haddock. Don't be taken aback by the high oven temperature as this it what gives the fish a nice, crispy crunch. I cook mine for 12 or 13 minutes and serve it with lemon wedges. This one is fool proof; try it, you'll love it!!!
This was really easy to prepare and it was really tasty! Instead of using the milk to coat the fish, I thought it would be easier to use egg.

Delicious. Changed salt to 1/2 garlic salt 1/2 sea salt. Soaked fish in milk for 10 minutes then proceeded to coat. Needed 2 pans, the metal pan made for a crisper fish coating. Easy recipe with great results.

I made this twice, the first time I made it exactly to the recipe it was OK but just using milk I found the breadcrumbs just didn't stick well to the fillets. I also found that the bread crumbs didn't brown as much as I thought. So I tweaked the recipe as follows, Tweak 1. I added 2 Tbsp of vegetable oil to the breadcrumbs mixed until thoroughly coated, I then placed them into a microwave for 1-3 minutes to give the browning process a little help. I then placed them into a shallow pan to cool. Instead of using milk I made a simple batter with eggs and flour. This was a huge improvement to get the breadcrumbs to stick to the fillets. The original recipe was a fantastic staring point though.

The temp works great(10 min). I turned off oven and left door open while finishing baked potatoes in the air fryer. I used crushed Ritz crackers instead of bread crumbs. Dusted lightly with Old Bay,garlic powder, and a little smoked paprika. Didn't add salt to the milk. Actually just beat an egg with a teaspoon or two of whole milk. Pretty darn good. Did the melted butter before the oven. Also I just used a cookie sheet with a wire rack for the fish.

Wow. Really good. My onion powder was a rock, so I doubled the garlic. Much less salt than the recipe called for...extra parm which is already salty. Dipped the fish 2 x to get lots of panko crumbs and put the leftover crumbs on top., the the melted butter. Convection Breville toaster oven @ 450 for 7 minutes on a sprayed grate. No pictures because we ate it right away. Definitely a keeper!

This was absolutely wonderful. Here are some small changes I made: I used only 1 teaspoon of salt in the milk, and instead of just dipping the fish in the milk, I let it soak in the milk while I prepared other things; I used panko crumbs; and I added some lemon pepper to the crumbs. Everything else stayed the same, and this was the best baked haddock I’ve ever had. Simple and delicious. Thanks for posting.

I made this with 1 lb. of haddock, (like Exeter Joe) omitted the milk, added white wine to the bottom of the baking dish. Put the fish in, added salt, pepper, garlic powder & paprika on top. Then I mixed some olive oil into whole wheat Panko crumbs and put that on top of the seasoned fish, eliminating the need for butter. Baked about 20 minutes at 445 degrees, or until Panko looked crispy. Delicious!

this is the only way I will make halibut. I lined a pan with foil, put a rack in the pan, sprayed with canola spray. I dipped he fish in whisked egg, then pressed the fish into a a spiced rub and panok, poured melted butter on top, baked for 15 minutes at 500 degrees, squeezed fresh lemon and served.................so good

This was a good baked fish recipe. I made a few changes. I added some Old Bay seasoning to the milk. Also, knowing that the bottom of the fish was going to get soggy, I breaded only the top of the fish. And because of a diet restriction, I skipped the butter and sprayed the breaded top with avocado oil spray instead. My fish was done in 12 minutes at 500F.
Oh man, I love this recipe! Only changed the spice to italian seasoning for I didn't have thyme, I will definitely make this again and again!!
Best haddock recipe yet! Melts in your mouth..!
Super easy and delish!
Easy and delicious
Simplicity at its best! Followed recipe exactly as written. I wouldn’t change a thing. Easy, Quick, & Delicious. Enjoy
This was amazing!

Made it mostly as written; just took a little advice from other reviewers and used egg instead of milk, put a rack in the bottom of the baking dish to keep the fillet bottoms from getting soggy, and finished it off with a squeeze of lemon. The results were great; crispy on the outside and moist and flaky on the inside. The lemon really wakes it up. I'd recommend using fresh fish if you can get it and grating your own Parmesan. With a recipe this simple, using the best ingredients is key. I'll definitely make this one again. It's a lot of flavor for minimal effort.. Thanks for posting!
Absolutely delicious my husband loved it definitely a keeper
Excellent. So easy to follow. Used some panko bread crumbs and regular bread crumbs. Came really crispy.. Husband approved!! Perfect recipe for haddock
